purpose: How a plating-bench operator turns a specified gold thickness into a delivered one: estimating the true cathode area, choosing current density inside the TDS window, converting amps and minutes into an expected thickness by Faraday arithmetic honestly scaled by cathode efficiency, proving the rectifier before trusting it, steering current distribution on real jewelry shapes with shields, robbers and auxiliary-anode classes, and closing every run with measurement so the estimate is always corrected by the deposit itself.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the piece arrives prepped and the bath arrives healthy: surface preparation, bath selection and bath maintenance are owned by upstream specialists and are trusted inputs here

all plating chemistry is a purchased commercial product operated per its supplier technical data sheet (TDS); every numeric operating window in this KB is a mechanism or a handbook-class reference, never an asserted setpoint
the layer stack (strike, underplates, top coat) is specified by the layer-architecture plan before this KB's work begins; this KB delivers the specified microns of the layer being plated
workplace electrical, chemical and waste rules vary by jurisdiction and must be verified locally; safety statements here are obligation classes plus formal-training pointers, not procedures
exclusions: stack design: strike-layer selection, barrier underplates (nickel, palladium, white bronze, copper leveling), diffusion and migration mechanisms, flash-vs-heavy build choices per wear class, duplex systems and post-plate topcoats belong to the layer-architecture KB; this KB consumes the finished stack spec and passes its nickel-release compliance flag through untouched

physical run handling: rack vs barrel vs brush decisions, wiring and contact-point placement, hiding contact marks, agitation hardware and part positioning, drag-out management, inter-tank rinse sequence, post-plate dry and first-touch handling, and full job logging belong to the fixturing-and-run-handling KB; this KB states the electrical requirements the load plan must satisfy and contributes the ampere-minute column to the run log

bath chemistry: choosing a gold system, analyzing and replenishing it, and diagnosing contamination belong to the bath-chemistry specialist; this KB treats gold content and additive state as given bath health

numeric setpoints asserted as fact: current density, temperature, time and efficiency figures are taught as mechanisms and handbook-class ranges; the specific product TDS and the shop's own logged runs govern actual numbers

mains-side electrical work, rectifier internals, bypassing fuses or interlocks, or any rigging outside the equipment manufacturer's instructions: that work goes to a qualified electrician, never the plating bench

regulated marking terms (gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold) and nickel-release limits as numeric thresholds: they appear only as compliance classes with a verify-your-jurisdiction obligation; claim approval belongs to the marking-compliance specialist
forcing a piece that cannot be racked or contacted without damage: that piece is escalated to intake and the customer decision path, never improvised onto the line
personalized legal, medical or financial advice, including nickel-allergy guidance, which routes to regulation classes and professional care

competency_questions.question: What exactly is this job's thickness target, where on the piece must it be met, and which wear and marking classes does it invoke?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THICKNESS_TARGET_SPEC yields a written microns target with named measurement points, a wear-class assignment, and marking-class plus nickel-release flags carried as verify-jurisdiction classes

competency_questions.question: When the handbook, the supplier TDS and my own habit disagree on a number, which one governs and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDS_AND_LOG_AUTHORITY ranks the specific product TDS plus the shop's logged runs above handbook-class ranges and above operator habit, with handbook figures allowed only as orientation classes

competency_questions.question: How do I estimate the plated surface area of this load, and what happens downstream when the estimate is wrong?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SURFACE_AREA_ESTIMATION names at least geometric decomposition, weight-and-gauge arithmetic, and reference-piece comparison, includes robbers and exposed rack in the count, and states that area error converts one-for-one into current-density error

competency_questions.question: What does current density do to the deposit when it is too high and when it is too low, and what moves the usable window?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_DENSITY_MASTER describes burn (dark, rough, stressed deposits at edges) above the limiting current and slow, dull, poorly covering deposits when starved low, and AGITATION_LIMITING_CURRENT explains that agitation, gold content and temperature move the window

competency_questions.question: How do I turn amps, minutes and area into an expected thickness, and why is that number an estimate until measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FARADAY_TIME_THICKNESS shows charge-to-mass-to-thickness through area and gold density scaled by efficiency, and CATHODE_EFFICIENCY_REALITY explains why efficiency is a bath-family class band that drifts and must be calibrated by measurement

competency_questions.question: How do I set up the rectifier for a run and prove it is telling the truth before parts go in?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECTIFIER_SETUP_CC specifies constant-current mode with amps sized from current density times area per the manufacturer's manual, and RECTIFIER_VERIFICATION requires polarity, meter and delivered-current checks before the first live entry

competency_questions.question: Where on this specific piece will current pile up and where will it starve, and how do I know before plating?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_DISTRIBUTION_MAP predicts hot edges, tips and outer curves versus starved recesses, bores and shadowed zones from geometry and anode placement, and turns the prediction into marked thick/thin zones and measurement points

competency_questions.question: What do I do when the same piece has edges that want to burn and recesses that want to starve?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HCD_ZONE_CONTROL and LCD_ZONE_CONTROL give the mitigation options for each zone and SHIELDS_AND_ROBBERS supplies the passive tools, with the conflict resolved by plating for the starved zone's floor while protecting hot zones

competency_questions.question: When does a geometry need an auxiliary or conforming anode, and what classes of auxiliary anode and anode material are legitimate in gold work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUX_ANODE_CLASSES distinguishes auxiliary, conforming and internal anodes as classes, names insoluble anode material classes (platinized titanium, mixed-metal-oxide titanium) and forbids improvised bare steel or stainless in acid gold

competency_questions.question: What must be true electrically at the instant a piece enters gold, and what do I watch while it plates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LIVE_ENTRY_DISCIPLINE requires verified current flowing before immersion to prevent immersion deposits, and CELL_VOLTAGE_SANITY uses the constant-current voltage reading as the in-run diagnostic for contacts, anodes and area errors

competency_questions.question: How do I prove the thickness I delivered, where do I measure, and how does each measurement improve the next estimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: XRF_FIRST_ARTICLE requires a first-article reading at the mapped worst point plus high-wear points before the batch continues, WITNESS_COUPON_WEIGHT_GAIN supplies the coupon and weight-gain cross-check that calibrates efficiency, and AMPERE_MINUTE_LEDGER ties the delivered charge to the result

competency_questions.question: Which electrical work may I do at the bench, and where is the hard line that sends work to a qualified electrician?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELECTRICAL_SAFETY_BOUNDARY keeps bench work inside equipment manufacturer instructions, sends mains-side and internal work to a qualified electrician, names the mains-plus-heaters-plus-liquid combination as the hazard class, and points to formal training and jurisdiction rules

competency_questions.question: What does overshooting or undershooting the thickness target cost, and how do I trim delivery honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOLD_ECONOMY_OF_THICKNESS derives gold mass from area times thickness times gold density as the overshoot cost mechanism, names undershoot as spec failure and rework, and permits trimming only above a measured worst-point floor

competency_questions.question: When do I stop trying to control current on a geometry and escalate the piece instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GEOMETRY_ESCALATION_BOUNDARY triggers escalation to intake and the customer decision path when recesses cannot reach the spec floor within the shop's equipment class or the piece cannot be contacted without damage, with the attempted mitigations documented

glossary.definition: Amperes delivered per unit of immersed cathode area (commonly amps per square decimeter at the bench); the master variable of electrodeposition, because deposit structure, brightness, stress and efficiency all respond to it rather than to total amps.

The current density at which gold ions can no longer diffuse to the cathode surface as fast as charge arrives; above it the deposit burns (dark, rough, stressed) and efficiency collapses. It rises with agitation, gold concentration and temperature, which is why the same amps can burn one day and run clean the next.

A chemistry's ability to deposit comparable thickness in low-current-density zones relative to high ones; good throwing power softens the thick-edge thin-recess pattern, poor throwing power exaggerates it, and no chemistry eliminates it on deep geometry.

The fraction of delivered charge that actually becomes deposited gold rather than side reactions such as hydrogen evolution; alkaline cyanide soft golds run near-quantitative while acid hard golds run far lower and drift with bath age, so the honest value for a given tank is measured, not assumed.

One ampere flowing for one minute; the natural bookkeeping unit of electrodeposited thickness, because deposited mass is proportional to charge. Logged ampere-minutes per load are both the thickness ledger and the replenishment driver.

Entering the work into the gold bath with current already flowing; prevents the spontaneous displacement (immersion) gold film that forms on a less-noble surface at open circuit, which has near-zero adhesion and peels later from under an otherwise good deposit.

A sacrificial cathode (often a wire loop or strip) placed near a high-current-density feature to steal current away from it; it lowers local current density on the work but adds cathode area and consumes gold, so it must be counted in the area estimate.

An extra anode brought close to a starved zone to raise its local current density; the conforming variant is shaped to follow the work's geometry, and the internal variant reaches down a bore or inside a hollow. All are rigged with insulated leads within the equipment's instructions.

A small piece of known area racked with the load and plated under the same conditions; measured afterward by weight gain or XRF it reveals the tank's real deposition rate and efficiency at those settings, calibrating future Faraday estimates.

X-ray fluorescence measurement of coating thickness (ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 method class); fast and non-destructive, but the calibration must match the actual layer stack and base metal, and very thin flash sits near the method's floor, so it is a method class with limits, not an oracle.

nodes.definition: Before any current flows, fix in writing what this job's 'plated' means: the gold thickness in microns, the points on the piece where it must be met, and the wear class it serves. Trade practice spans decorative flash coats, micron-class everyday plating and heavy-wear build, and published class structures (ISO 27874 jewelry gold-coating classes, ASTM B488 engineering types, the trade's flash/micron/heavy bands) are referenced strictly as named classes, never as invented numbers of our own. 'Vermeil' and 'gold plated' are regulated marking classes to be verified in the selling jurisdiction before any label claim. The spec inherits the stack from the layer-architecture plan, and whenever that stack contains nickel for skin-contact goods it carries the nickel-release compliance flag forward. Because delivery is judged at the worst point, the spec names its measurement points explicitly - the high-wear zones and the mapped worst recess - so 'on target' is checkable instead of arguable.

included: written microns target with named measurement points
wear-class assignment per job
marking-class and nickel-release flags carried as verify-jurisdiction classes
excluded: designing the layer stack (layer-architecture KB)
approving marking claims (marking-compliance specialist)
quoting the job (business specialist)

pros.claim: A written microns-and-points target turns 'make it gold' into a checkable delivery and ends disputes before they start
pros.example: a ring job specified as heavy-wear class at the shank with measurement at the shank outer face and prong backs is either met or not - no argument at handover

cons.claim: Specifying a floor at every point of an ornate piece can make the job undeliverable at any sane price
cons.example: demanding full micron thickness inside a filigree pendant's deepest recesses may require rigging the shop cannot do, forcing escalation rather than a quiet compromise

failure_modes: accepting 'gold plate it' with no microns and no measurement points, so delivery is judged by mood at handover
using a marking word like vermeil in the spec without the verify-jurisdiction flag
dropping the nickel-release compliance flag when copying the stack spec into the job sheet
acceptance_tests: the job sheet states microns, wear class, named measurement points including the mapped worst point, and any marking-class or nickel-release flags before racking begins
revisit_triggers: the customer changes the wear expectation or the selling jurisdiction after quoting
the distribution map shows the named worst point cannot reach the floor

base.update_signal: a delivered job disputed at handover despite meeting the written spec, or a jurisdiction ruling that changes what a named marking class requires

nodes.definition: Settle, once and for all jobs, where numbers come from. The supplier technical data sheet of the specific commercial bath defines the legitimate operating window - current density range, temperature, agitation class, replenishment scheme - and the shop's own logged runs refine where inside that window this tank on this bench actually performs. Published handbook figures (soft gold near-quantitative efficiency, acid hard gold's low-efficiency band, minutes-per-micron classes) are orientation references only, and operator habit carried over from a previous bath is not a source at all. When TDS, handbook and habit disagree, the TDS plus the log govern. The practical skill is reading a TDS window and translating it to this tank: identifying which end of the current-density range suits rack work at this agitation, what the replenishment bookkeeping expects, and which of the shop's logged baselines still apply after a bath change.

included: ranking TDS plus shop log above handbook classes and habit
reading a TDS operating window into bench settings
retiring stale log baselines when the product changes
excluded: bath analysis and replenishment execution (bath-chemistry specialist)
asserting any numeric window as universal fact

pros.claim: TDS-first discipline kills folklore numbers that quietly wreck deposits when products change
pros.example: the habit of 'run it at three volts like the old bath' dies the day the new product's TDS shows a current-controlled window that three volts would overdrive on small loads

cons.claim: A TDS window is wide and a young log is thin, so early runs on a new product carry real uncertainty
cons.example: the first week on a new hard gold means conservative mid-window current choices and a first-article measurement on every batch until the log grows teeth

failure_modes: porting an efficiency habit or current setting across bath families because the color of the solution looks the same
treating a handbook-class range as a setpoint instead of an orientation reference
keeping stale log baselines alive after a TDS revision or product swap
acceptance_tests: every numeric setting on the run sheet cites either the product TDS or a dated shop-log baseline, and no setting cites habit or a handbook figure alone
revisit_triggers: the supplier issues a TDS revision or the shop switches bath product
the log shows a systematic offset between TDS-window expectations and measured results on this tank

base.update_signal: a supplier TDS revision, a bath-product change, or a run of first-article measurements that contradicts the current window translation for this tank

nodes.definition: The hard boundary around electrical work at a plating bench. Rectifiers, immersion heaters and any auxiliary rigging are installed and used within their manufacturers' instructions; mains-side work, opening equipment, bypassing fuses or interlocks, paralleling outputs the manual does not sanction, and improvised heater wiring are out of bounds and go to a qualified electrician. The low-voltage DC side at plating currents is the benign part of the room; the dangerous combination is mains power plus immersion heaters plus conductive liquids plus wet hands, which is a shock-and-fire class demanding residual-current protection as an equipment class, dry-hands discipline, intact cords, and no daisy-chained power strips near tanks. This is obligation-class content with a formal-training pointer: verify your jurisdiction's workplace electrical rules, and treat every instruction here as subordinate to the equipment manual and local law, never a substitute for either.

included: bench-side use of rectifiers and rigging within manufacturer instructions
the mains-plus-heat-plus-liquid hazard class and its discipline
the hand-off line to a qualified electrician
formal-training and verify-jurisdiction pointers
excluded: any mains-side or internal equipment procedure
chemical safety classes beyond their electrical touchpoints (safety-compliance specialist)

pros.claim: A bright line between bench work and electrician work removes the deadliest improvisation channel from the room
pros.example: when a run needs more amps than the rectifier offers, the answer is split the load or schedule a second run - never a second supply jumpered onto the same bars against the manual

cons.claim: Respecting equipment limits sometimes costs real throughput on heavy loads
cons.example: a full rack of bangles that exceeds the supply's rated output waits for two runs even with the customer on the phone

failure_modes: treating the low-voltage DC side's harmlessness as permission to improvise on the mains side
running heaters and rectifiers on unprotected or daisy-chained circuits beside open tanks
letting deadline pressure reclassify electrician work as bench work
acceptance_tests: every electrical task performed at the bench can be pointed to in an equipment manual, and every task that cannot is documented as referred out
tank-side circuits carry residual-current protection as an equipment class and the emergency cutoff location is known to every operator
revisit_triggers: new equipment arrives with different instructions or ratings
any electrical near-miss, tripped protection event, or scorched connector at the bench

base.update_signal: an incident report, an equipment manual change, or a jurisdiction rule change touching workplace electrical practice near process tanks

nodes.definition: Estimate the true cathode area of the racked load, because every ampere decision divides by it. The bench methods are: geometric decomposition of pieces into bands, discs, cylinders and cones summed with a both-sides correction; CAD or supplier area data when the piece has a drawing; weight-and-gauge arithmetic for wire and sheet stock (mass and density give length and area); and comparison against a reference piece whose area was established before. The count includes everything that will draw current - every piece, any current robber, and any exposed rack tip or wire above the insulation - and applies the corrections everyone forgets: inner surfaces, holes, the backs of pendants. Area error converts one-for-one into current-density error: a load estimated at half its true area gets set at half the intended amps and starves, and a load estimated at double burns its edges at 'correct' settings. The estimate is written with its method and an honest error band, because the band decides how conservative the current choice must be.

included: geometric decomposition, CAD/supplier data, weight-and-gauge arithmetic, reference-piece comparison
counting robbers and exposed rack as cathode
stating method and error band with the estimate
excluded: choosing rack vs barrel or physical load layout (fixturing KB)
pricing gold content from area (business specialist)

pros.claim: A ten-minute decomposition gets most jewelry within a usable error band and makes the amp setting defensible
pros.example: a curb chain estimated by weight-and-gauge lands close enough that the mid-window current choice absorbs the residual error

cons.claim: Ornate, hollow or repousse work defeats clean geometry and can hide half its true area
cons.example: a hollow locket with a pierced front carries far more surface than its silhouette suggests, so it goes by reference-piece comparison or gets a witness coupon to calibrate the run

failure_modes: estimating the silhouette instead of the surface and starving the load at half-true-area amps
forgetting that a fitted current robber is cathode area that shifted the total
counting pieces instead of area when ring sizes in the batch vary widely
acceptance_tests: the run sheet shows the area estimate, the method used, the robber and rack allowance, and an error band before any current is chosen
revisit_triggers: any piece is added to or removed from the load after the estimate
a robber or auxiliary fixture is fitted or removed
first-article thickness misses in a way area error would explain

base.update_signal: a first-article measurement pattern that tracks area-estimate error, or a new load type (hollow, pierced, mixed-size) the current methods band poorly

nodes.definition: Current density - amps per unit of immersed cathode area - is the one knob that decides deposit quality, and the bench converts it to a rectifier setting by the rule total amps equal chosen current density times estimated area. Too high, above the limiting current the bath's diffusion can feed, the deposit goes dark and burnt at edges and tips, turns rough and stressed, and in acid gold the already-low efficiency collapses further, wasting time and charge. Too low, deposition crawls, job time balloons, coverage on less-noble spots of the surface can suffer, and color can drift off the retained standard. The workable window belongs to the product TDS; what the operator owns is positioning inside it: lower when agitation is weak, the load is uncertain, or the geometry has hot features; higher only when agitation, gold content and temperature genuinely support it. Chasing schedule by exceeding the window is how a batch is burned at 'only ten percent more amps'.

included: what high and low current density each do to the deposit
amps equal current density times area as the bench conversion
positioning inside the TDS window per agitation, load and geometry
excluded: asserting numeric windows (TDS territory)
bath-side causes of a shrunken window like depleted gold (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: Controlling current density rather than voltage or total amps makes results portable across loads of different size
pros.example: the same density that plated yesterday's six rings cleanly plates today's twenty when the amps are recomputed from the new area - copying yesterday's amps instead would starve the bigger load

cons.claim: Density is only as good as the area estimate and agitation reality underneath it
cons.example: a perfectly chosen density burns prong tips anyway when the stirrer coupling slipped and nobody re-derated the current

failure_modes: setting amps by habit from the last job instead of recomputing from this load's area
answering deadline pressure by pushing above the TDS window instead of raising agitation or accepting the run time
ignoring that the window moved down when gold content fell or agitation weakened
acceptance_tests: the run sheet derives amps from a stated density inside the TDS window times the stated area, with a note on where in the window and why
burn watch at first inspection shows no dark or matte zones at edges and tips
revisit_triggers: agitation, temperature or bath analysis changes since the density was chosen
burn or starvation symptoms appear at a setting that previously ran clean
the TDS window changes with a product or revision change

base.update_signal: recurring burn or starvation at settings the window sanctions, or shop-log evidence that this tank's usable window sits offset from the TDS orientation

nodes.definition: Cathode efficiency is the fraction of delivered charge that becomes gold instead of side reactions, and it is the number that separates bath families: alkaline cyanide soft gold runs near-quantitative as a handbook-class band, while acid hard gold runs in a low band that falls further with bath age and rising current density - which is why the same ampere-minutes deliver a micron in one tank and a fraction of it in another. The efficiency of this tank today is unknown until measured; it drifts with bath age, contamination, current density, temperature and additive state, so any stored factor decays. The bench discipline is threefold: never carry an efficiency habit across bath families; hold a per-tank calibrated factor with a date on it; and let every witness coupon or first-article measurement update that factor. An efficiency assumption is the single most common reason a Faraday time estimate delivers half the specified thickness while looking perfectly rigorous on paper.

included: efficiency as a bath-family class band
drift with age, density, temperature and contamination as mechanisms
the per-tank dated calibration factor
excluded: diagnosing why efficiency fell (bath-chemistry specialist)
asserting a numeric efficiency for any tank without measurement

pros.claim: A dated per-tank efficiency factor turns Faraday arithmetic from folklore into a usable estimator
pros.example: after three coupon calibrations, the hard gold tank's factor predicts first-article thickness within the check band, so batch time quotes stop being guesses

cons.claim: The factor is a snapshot that ages with the bath, and trusting an old one reintroduces the original error
cons.example: a factor calibrated at bath make-up quietly overstates deposition three months of ampere-hours later, and the shortfall surfaces as thin prong backs at final inspection

failure_modes: applying a soft-gold near-quantitative habit to an acid hard gold tank and delivering half thickness
using an undated factor with no note of the density and temperature it was calibrated at
letting a single flattering coupon overwrite a factor instead of trending it
acceptance_tests: the efficiency factor used in any time estimate carries a calibration date, the settings it was measured at, and the bath family it belongs to
revisit_triggers: bath analysis or a maintenance event (carbon treatment, replenishment overhaul) changes the tank's state
measured-versus-estimated thickness gap widens across consecutive first articles
current density or temperature moves away from where the factor was calibrated

base.update_signal: each witness coupon or first-article result, which either confirms the current factor or moves it; a bath family change resets the factor entirely

nodes.definition: Turn electricity into an expected thickness, honestly. Deposited mass follows charge by Faraday's law - for monovalent gold a fixed mass per ampere-minute at perfect efficiency - and thickness follows from mass divided by plated area times gold's density of 19.3 g/cm3, scaled down by the tank's calibrated cathode efficiency. The bench form is minutes-per-micron at the chosen current density: near-quantitative soft gold plates a micron several times faster than low-efficiency acid hard gold at comparable density, and both are handbook-class relationships whose actual value for this tank comes from the calibrated factor. The output is an estimate with a band, not a promise: it sets the planned run time and the ampere-minute budget, and it is verified by first-article measurement every batch, because efficiency drift, area error and distribution effects all hide inside it. An estimate that has not been checked against a measured deposit is scheduling information, never a thickness claim.

included: charge to mass to thickness through area, density and efficiency
minutes-per-micron as a mechanism with class-range orientation
the estimate-with-band output and its verification obligation
excluded: thickness claims to customers (verification and marking specialists)
asserting a universal minutes-per-micron number

pros.claim: Faraday arithmetic gives a principled run time and replenishment budget before any gold is spent
pros.example: sizing a heavy-wear ring run from area, chosen density and the dated efficiency factor lands the first article near the floor, and the trim to spec is minutes, not another full run

cons.claim: The formula's precision flatters inputs that are themselves estimates, and the neat number invites false confidence
cons.example: a beautifully computed 40-minute run still delivers thin recesses because the formula predicts average thickness while the spec is judged at the mapped worst point

failure_modes: treating the computed thickness as delivered thickness and skipping the first article
quoting the estimate to a customer as a guarantee
using average-thickness math against a worst-point spec without a distribution allowance
acceptance_tests: every time estimate shows its area, density, efficiency factor with date, and an expected band, and is labeled unverified until a first-article measurement closes it
revisit_triggers: the efficiency factor, area estimate or chosen density changes after the estimate was made
first-article results land outside the estimate's band two batches running

base.update_signal: the running gap between estimated and measured thickness across the shop log; a persistent bias means the estimator's inputs, not the arithmetic, need repair

nodes.definition: Set the supply up the way electrodeposition wants it, per its own manual: constant-current mode, because thickness is charge-controlled and the cell voltage should fall where the chemistry and geometry put it; amps sized from chosen current density times estimated area; work connected cathodic with polarity double-checked, since reversed polarity strips or dissolves instead of plating; leads and clips sized and clean so contact resistance does not eat the budget; and a low-ripple output class, because heavily rippled current degrades bright deposits. Constant-voltage habit is the classic trap: at fixed voltage the current wanders as the bath warms and the load changes, so the delivered charge - and therefore the thickness - becomes unknown. Where the manual sanctions multiple output circuits or bars, current sharing follows its instructions, never improvised jumpering. Everything here stays on the bench side of the electrical safety boundary: setup uses the controls and terminals the manufacturer provides, and anything beyond them is referred out.

included: constant-current mode rationale and setup
amps from density times area
polarity, lead and ripple-class checks per the manual
excluded: internal repair or mains-side work (qualified electrician)
physical contact placement on pieces (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: Constant-current mode makes the thickness math mean something for the whole run
pros.example: at set amps the ampere-minute ledger is literally minutes times the dial, while the constant-voltage habit would have let current climb as the tank warmed and quietly overplate the afternoon batches

cons.claim: Constant current will force voltage up over a failing contact and hide it from a casual glance at the ammeter
cons.example: the panel still reads the set amps while a corroded clip drops volts and one rack arm's pieces run at double density - the voltage reading, not the current reading, tells that story

failure_modes: running constant-voltage out of habit so delivered charge is unknown
reversed polarity stripping a strike or dissolving work into the bath
undersized or dirty leads turning the amp budget into heat at the clips
acceptance_tests: before entry the setup record shows constant-current mode selected, the amp setting derived on the run sheet, and polarity verified at the work bar
revisit_triggers: the load, robber fit or bar arrangement changes after setup
cell voltage at set current departs from this job class's logged typical band

base.update_signal: a run where delivered charge disagreed with the dial-times-time expectation, or new supply hardware whose manual changes the sanctioned setup

nodes.definition: Prove the panel tells the truth before trusting it with gold. A rectifier that reads amps it is not delivering - or delivers amps it does not read - corrupts every Faraday estimate, every ampere-minute ledger line, and every logged baseline the shop will later lean on, all while looking perfectly normal. The verification discipline, performed within the manufacturer's procedures: zero the meters and check them at rest; compare the panel ammeter against an independent clamp meter or external shunt at working current; confirm the set current is actually delivered into a dummy load or scrap cathode before the first real entry of the day; verify polarity at the work bar, not just at the panel lamp; and keep a dated verification cadence in the log so drift is caught on schedule rather than by ruined batches. Metering faults are insidious precisely because constant-current mode keeps the display serene while the calibration underneath it walks away.

included: meter zero and independent cross-check
delivered-versus-set current confirmation on a dummy load
polarity verification at the bar
dated verification cadence
excluded: opening the unit or adjusting internal calibration (qualified service)
daily bath verification (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: A five-minute morning verification protects every number the rest of the day produces
pros.example: catching a panel ammeter reading a fifth high at the clamp meter saves the whole day's batches from silent underplating and the log from poisoned baselines

cons.claim: Verification takes discipline precisely because it almost always passes
cons.example: after a year of green checks the morning shunt comparison feels like ritual - which is exactly when a drifted meter finally arrives and pays for every skipped day

failure_modes: trusting the panel because the deposit 'looks right' at a glance
verifying once at installation and never again
checking polarity at the panel indicator while the bars are swapped downstream
acceptance_tests: the log shows a dated verification entry - meter cross-check, delivered-current confirmation, polarity at the bar - before the first live entry after any idle period or hardware change
revisit_triggers: measured thickness disagrees with the ampere-minute ledger in a way meter error would explain
any lead, clip, shunt or supply hardware is replaced

base.update_signal: a verification failure, a ledger-versus-measurement discrepancy, or a manufacturer service bulletin on the metering

nodes.definition: Predict where current will pile up and where it will starve before the piece ever enters the tank. Electric field concentrates on edges, tips, points and outer curves - the high-current-density zones that plate thick and burn first - and thins into recesses, bores, inner surfaces and anything shadowed from the anode - the low-current-density zones that plate thin and starve. Primary distribution is set by geometry and anode placement; the chemistry's throwing power moderates it but never erases it on deep jewelry geometry. The bench artifact is a marked-up map of the actual piece: expected hot features, expected starved zones, the worst point named, and from it three decisions flow - where shields, robbers or auxiliary anodes are needed, where the spec's measurement points must sit, and whether this geometry can reach its floor at all within the shop's equipment class or must be escalated. A batch is mapped by its worst piece, not its average one.

included: hot-zone and starved-zone prediction from geometry and anode placement
throwing power as moderator
the marked map naming the worst point
excluded: physical positioning and racking execution (fixturing KB)
computational field simulation beyond bench judgment

pros.claim: Ten minutes of mapping converts burn-and-starve surprises into planned mitigations
pros.example: marking a claw-set ring's prong tips as hot and the under-gallery as starved before the run puts a robber loop and the XRF probe exactly where they belong

cons.claim: Bench prediction is qualitative and can misrank zones on genuinely novel geometry
cons.example: a pierced dome's interior lattice may starve worse than the map guessed, which is why the first article measures the mapped worst point and demotes the map when it is wrong

failure_modes: mapping the batch by its easiest piece and letting the ornate ones ride
placing measurement points on convenient flats instead of mapped worst zones
treating good throwing power as a license to skip mapping deep recesses
acceptance_tests: each job's map names hot features, starved zones and the worst point, and the spec's measurement points cover that worst point
revisit_triggers: first-article readings contradict the mapped ranking of zones
anode arrangement, tank geometry or load layout changes
a new piece family (hollow, pierced, deep-recess) enters the shop's work mix

base.update_signal: accumulated first-article evidence on which zone predictions hold for the shop's actual piece families and which need re-ranking

nodes.definition: Keep the hot zones below the burn threshold. Prong tips, sharp edges, outer curves and the pieces nearest the anode see current density well above the load average, and they announce trouble early: a matte, then brown, then dark rough deposit at exactly those features while the rest still looks fine. The control options, in the order a bench usually reaches for them: drop total current so the hottest zone falls back inside the window; raise agitation within what the TDS and the mist-safety line allow, which lifts the limiting current everywhere; increase anode-to-work distance or reposition so the field spreads; and fit a shield or robber to take the specific feature out of the firing line. What ignoring it costs: a burned zone is not a cosmetic note - the deposit there is rough, stressed and often poorly adherent, and the honest remedy is strip and replate, which spends gold twice and risks the piece. Early burn recognized at first inspection is a settings correction; burn discovered at final inspection is rework.

included: early burn recognition at hot features
the mitigation ladder: current, agitation, distance, shield or robber
the strip-and-replate consequence
excluded: full defect cause trees after release (quality specialist)
agitation hardware changes (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: Catching burn at its first matte hint on the hottest feature saves the batch at the cost of a settings tweak
pros.example: spotting dulling prong tips two minutes in, dropping current and adding a robber loop finishes the run clean instead of stripping six rings

cons.claim: Every hot-zone mitigation trades something: current costs time, distance costs tank space, robbers cost gold and area math
cons.example: the robber that saves the prongs adds cathode area that must be recounted, and the lower current adds twenty minutes to the run the schedule did not have

failure_modes: reading early matte edges as 'it will bright up' and letting the burn set in
fixing burn by dropping current so far the recesses starve instead
fitting a robber and never updating the area and amp arithmetic
acceptance_tests: first inspection during the run explicitly checks the mapped hottest features, and any mitigation applied is recorded with its area and current consequences
revisit_triggers: burn recurs at settings that previously ran clean, pointing at agitation, analysis or area drift

base.update_signal: the shop's burn-incident pattern: which features, which settings, which mitigations held - fed back into the mapping defaults

nodes.definition: Get the starved zones to the spec floor, because that is where the spec is actually judged. Recesses, bores, under-galleries and shadowed inner surfaces receive a fraction of the average current density, plate proportionally thin, and in extreme starvation plate patchy or off-color - and none of this shows in an average or convenient-flat measurement. The control options: bring an auxiliary or conforming anode class close to the starved zone; reposition the work or the anodes so the shadow opens; accept a longer run at lower current so the recess accumulates thickness while shields protect the hot zones; and in every case put the measurement point in the worst zone so the delivery is proven, not presumed. When the floor genuinely cannot be reached within the shop's equipment class, the honest outputs are disclosure and escalation - a documented thin-zone waiver from the customer or a respec - never a quietly thin recess under a confidently thick shank.

included: starvation recognition and its invisibility to average readings
the mitigation set: auxiliary anode classes, repositioning, longer-slower runs
worst-point measurement and the disclose-or-escalate rule
excluded: auxiliary anode construction details beyond classes (equipment manuals)
customer negotiation itself (intake and business specialists)

pros.claim: Plating for the worst zone makes the delivered spec true everywhere instead of true on average
pros.example: sizing the run so a pendant's bail interior reaches the floor means the flat back is comfortably over it - the reverse plan leaves the bail bare in a year of wear

cons.claim: Worst-zone delivery costs gold and time on every easy zone of the same piece
cons.example: reaching the floor inside a deep under-gallery may put half a micron of surplus on the shank - cost the quote must carry or the geometry must escalate

failure_modes: declaring the piece on-spec from a flat-back reading while the recess sits at a fraction of the floor
compensating starvation with more total current and burning the edges instead
shipping a known-thin recess without disclosure because the visible surfaces measured well
acceptance_tests: the first article is measured in the mapped worst zone and meets the floor there, or the job shows a documented waiver or escalation before release
revisit_triggers: a recess measurement misses while flats pass, meaning the mitigation plan or the map needs rework
a new deep-geometry piece family arrives that the current auxiliary-anode capability cannot serve

base.update_signal: worst-zone measurement history: how often mapped recesses reach floor under each mitigation class, and which geometries keep failing

nodes.definition: The passive current-distribution tools, as classes. A shield is a non-conductive baffle - inert plastic sheet or strip sanctioned for the bath - placed between anode and work to shadow a hot feature, lowering its local current density without touching the piece or spending gold; its cost is that it also shadows whatever sits behind it. A robber (current thief) is a sacrificial cathode - typically a wire loop or strip - placed near a hot feature to steal current away; it protects delicate tips and edges well, but it is real cathode area that must enter the area estimate and it plates real gold that leaves as scrap value, not product. Both are placed empirically: map, fit, run, and let the first article judge the placement. The choice between them at the bench: shield when the hot zone is broad and gold cost matters; rob when the feature is small, sharp and precious. Both are re-declared on the run sheet whenever fitted, moved or removed, because a silent robber is a silent area error.

included: shield class and robber class, their mechanisms and costs
when each fits
the declare-on-run-sheet rule
excluded: rack construction and mounting hardware (fixturing KB)
active auxiliary anodes (their own node)

pros.claim: A well-placed robber lets one current setting serve a piece whose tips would otherwise burn before its body plated
pros.example: a wire loop around a marquise setting's point takes the burn while the crown and shank plate clean at the density the recesses needed

cons.claim: Every robber spends gold on scrap and every shield starves its own shadow
cons.example: the loop that saved the point carries gold to the scrap jar each run, and a carelessly wide shield behind it left a pale stripe on the neighboring piece

failure_modes: fitting a robber without adding its area to the estimate, so the whole load runs starved
shielding a hot zone and accidentally shadowing another piece behind it
leaving last job's robber on the rack into a job whose arithmetic never counted it
acceptance_tests: any shield or robber in the tank appears on the run sheet with the robber's area added to the estimate and the shield's shadow checked against neighboring work
revisit_triggers: first-article results show the protected feature still hot or the shadowed neighbor thin

base.update_signal: placement outcomes from first articles: which shield and robber geometries held for which features, accumulated into the shop's fitting habits

nodes.definition: The active tools for starved zones, as classes. An auxiliary anode is an extra anode brought close to a low-current-density zone to raise its local density; a conforming anode is shaped to follow the work's geometry at near-constant spacing; an internal anode reaches down a bore or into a hollow that no external field will ever serve. For gold work the anode material classes are the insoluble oxygen-evolving ones - platinized titanium and mixed-metal-oxide coated titanium - because gold is replenished from salt, not from the anode; improvised bare steel or stainless in an acid gold bath is a bath-poisoning event, dissolving iron, chromium and nickel into the chemistry. Auxiliary rigging is electrically real: insulated leads, secure connections above the solution line where the equipment class expects them, current shared per the supply's instructions, and the whole arrangement inside the electrical safety boundary. Anode-to-work spacing and anode area relative to the work are the mechanism levers - closer and larger raises the served zone's density - and the first article in the served zone judges the rig.

included: auxiliary, conforming and internal anode classes and when each is warranted
insoluble anode material classes for gold work
spacing and relative-area mechanisms
rigging within equipment instructions
excluded: anode fabrication beyond commercially available classes
bath-side anode chemistry management (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: An auxiliary anode reaches thickness into zones that no amount of patience at the main anodes will serve
pros.example: a short internal anode down a napkin-ring's bore delivers the interior floor in one run, where the external-only arrangement left the bore at a small fraction after double time

cons.claim: Every auxiliary anode is a new hot zone for whatever sits closest to it and a new failure point in the circuit
cons.example: the bore anode that fixed the interior burned the bore's entry lip until its tip was sleeved back from the mouth

failure_modes: dropping a stainless rod into acid gold as an improvised auxiliary and contaminating the bath
rigging an auxiliary with bare leads under the solution line outside the equipment's instructions
fitting an internal anode without re-planning current sharing, so the main circuit starves
acceptance_tests: any auxiliary anode in use is of an insoluble class sanctioned for the bath, appears in the current-sharing plan, and the zone it serves is a named measurement point on the first article
revisit_triggers: the served zone still misses floor, or a new adjacent burn appears after the rig is fitted

base.update_signal: served-zone first-article outcomes per rig class, and any bath-contamination incident traced to anode material choice

nodes.definition: Solution movement sets the ceiling on usable current density, and gold baths make the coupling unusually tight: acid hard gold runs metal-lean and diffusion-limited, so the rate at which agitation refreshes the depleted layer at the work surface directly determines the limiting current - stronger movement, higher ceiling; weaker movement, burn at yesterday's amps. The bench consequences: current density is chosen for the agitation actually running today, not the agitation the run sheet assumes; any agitation change - a slowed stirrer, a repositioned cathode rod, a fuller tank - re-derates the current before the next entry; and burn appearing at previously clean settings is read first as an agitation or gold-content question, not a rectifier one. One hard safety line crosses this node: cyanide-bearing baths are never air-sparged into mist - aerosolized cyanide solution is an exposure route - so agitation on those tanks is mechanical or solution-pumped per the TDS, and any agitation upgrade stays within the safety-compliance specialist's obligation classes. Hardware selection and placement belong to fixturing; what this node owns is the electrical consequence.

included: limiting current as a function of solution movement
re-derating current when agitation changes
the no-air-sparge line on cyanide baths as a safety class
excluded: agitation hardware choice and placement (fixturing KB)
ventilation and exposure-control procedure (safety-compliance specialist)

pros.claim: Reading agitation and current as one coupled setting explains burn incidents that meter-watching never will
pros.example: the batch that burned at the same amps as last week is solved at the stirrer whose coupling slipped, not at the rectifier that was never wrong

cons.claim: Agitation is the least instrumented variable on a small bench, so the coupling runs on judgment
cons.example: without a flow meter, 'moderate movement' is an operator's eye - which is why current choices near the window's top demand a witness of the first minutes

failure_modes: raising current to meet schedule without raising solution movement to carry it
air-sparging a cyanide gold bath for more agitation and creating a mist exposure route
leaving the current at full window after switching to a gentler agitation for delicate work
acceptance_tests: the run sheet's current choice names the agitation state it assumes, and any agitation change triggers a recorded re-derate before the next entry
revisit_triggers: burn at previously clean settings
any agitation hardware or placement change on the tank
a TDS or safety-class change touching allowable agitation methods

base.update_signal: burn-incident correlation with agitation state in the shop log, or a bath change that shifts how diffusion-limited the chemistry is

nodes.definition: Current is flowing before the work touches gold, every time. At open circuit a less-noble surface sitting in a gold electrolyte spontaneously trades metal for gold - a displacement (immersion) film with near-zero adhesion - and that film then sits under everything subsequently plated, waiting to peel weeks later under a deposit that looked perfect at release. The discipline is a fixed entry sequence: rectifier verified and set to the entry current, contact continuity to the work confirmed, current confirmed actually flowing (the ammeter moves as the work enters), then immersion - and the same applies at every gold tank in the sequence, strike and build alike. Which strike the stack uses is the layer-architecture plan's decision; that the entry into it is live is this node's. Transfer haste is the enemy: the seconds saved by hanging work first and reaching for the switch second are bought with an invisible interlayer that no inspection at release will catch. A dead entry discovered mid-run is not patched by plating longer; the honest path is back out, strip or re-activate per the stack's rules, and enter live.

included: the live-entry sequence and its verification
immersion-film formation as the failure mechanism
the back-out rule after a dead entry
excluded: strike selection and stack design (layer-architecture KB)
inter-tank transfer logistics and rinse sequence (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: A fixed entry ritual makes the invisible failure impossible rather than merely unlikely
pros.example: switch on, watch the ammeter kick as the rack enters, then let go - the habit costs three seconds and removes the peeling-next-month class of complaint entirely

cons.claim: Live entry at the set working current can overdrive delicate work in the first seconds on some chemistries
cons.example: where the TDS prescribes a gentler entry current before ramping to working density, the discipline follows the TDS - live entry means current flowing, not maximum current

failure_modes: hanging the work first and reaching for the switch second during a rushed transfer
assuming the strike tank's entry matters but the build tank's does not
plating over a suspected dead entry instead of backing out
acceptance_tests: the entry checklist - current set, continuity confirmed, ammeter response observed at immersion - is ticked for every gold-tank entry on the run sheet
revisit_triggers: any adhesion failure at or after release traced to an interlayer
a chemistry change whose TDS prescribes a different entry profile

base.update_signal: any delayed peeling complaint on released work, which reopens the entry discipline audit before it reopens anything else

nodes.definition: Under constant current, the voltage is the free diagnostic channel. The supply will push whatever volts it takes to hold the set amps, so the voltmeter tells the story the serene ammeter hides: a cell voltage in this tank's logged typical band for this job class means the circuit is as planned; abnormally high voltage means resistance where it should not be - a corroded clip, a failing contact, a passivated or fouled anode, or low bath conductivity; abnormally low voltage means current is finding an easier path - a short, a forgotten robber, or a load area far larger than estimated. Trending matters more than the absolute number: a slow climb during a run flags a contact cooking itself before its pieces come out half-plated on one side. The bench habit is to log the voltage at entry and at checks, hold a typical band per job class in the shop log, and treat any excursion as a stop-and-look, not a shrug. Cell voltage varies legitimately with geometry, spacing and bath state, which is exactly why the reference is this tank's own logged band and never a number from anywhere else.

included: voltage-at-constant-current as circuit diagnostic
high and low excursion readings and their causes
per-job-class typical bands from the shop log
excluded: fixing the physical contact (fixturing KB)
anode chemistry treatment (bath-chemistry specialist)
quoting voltage setpoints as facts

pros.claim: Voltage trending catches single-arm contact failures the ammeter cannot see
pros.example: total amps held all run, but the climbing volts flagged one rack arm going high-resistance - caught at mid-run check, its pieces were saved by reseating instead of discovered thin at XRF

cons.claim: Voltage is a many-caused signal and over-reading it invites wrong fixes
cons.example: a high reading blamed on the anode was actually the season's colder bath raising resistance - the log's typical band per conditions, not a single number, keeps the diagnostic honest

failure_modes: watching only the ammeter because current is what was set
having no logged typical band, so no reading is ever abnormal
continuing a run through a voltage excursion to protect the schedule
acceptance_tests: entry and mid-run voltage readings are logged against the job class's typical band, and any excursion shows a stop-and-look note
revisit_triggers: the typical band itself drifts across jobs, pointing at slow anode, contact or bath changes

base.update_signal: excursion incidents and their confirmed causes, which sharpen the shop's mapping from voltage signature to fault class

nodes.definition: The ampere-minute ledger is the electrical thickness ledger of the shop. Because deposited mass is proportional to charge, amps times minutes per load is the number that connects the plan to the deposit: it is the target the Faraday estimate sets, the running total the operator watches during the run, the input the gold-salt replenishment bookkeeping consumes per the TDS, and the line that lets a first-article measurement be translated into a corrected efficiency factor rather than a shrug. The bench practice: log set current and start time at entry, log interruptions honestly (a five-minute contact fix at zero current is zero ampere-minutes, not five minutes of plating), close the line at withdrawal, and reconcile against the measured thickness when the first article is read. Written during the run, the ledger is evidence; reconstructed afterward from memory, it is fiction that will poison the efficiency factor and the shop log both. The full job record - operator, bath, piece, prep - belongs to the run-handling KB; this ledger is the electrical column that feeds it.

included: per-load ampere-minute logging with honest interruptions
reconciliation against measured thickness
feeding replenishment bookkeeping per TDS
excluded: the full run log and job record (fixturing and run-handling KB)
executing replenishment (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: A live ledger turns every batch into a calibration point for the next one
pros.example: when the first article reads under estimate, the exact logged ampere-minutes let the shortfall become a corrected efficiency factor instead of a mystery

cons.claim: Ledger discipline is clerical work in a wet room and it degrades exactly when things get busy
cons.example: the interrupted run that resumed 'about ten minutes later' at an unlogged current is the ledger line that later makes the efficiency trend look insane

failure_modes: reconstructing the ledger after the fact from memory
logging wall-clock time across interruptions as if current flowed throughout
keeping the ledger but never reconciling it against measured thickness
acceptance_tests: each load's ledger line shows current, start, interruptions and close, written during the run, and carries the reconciliation note once the first article is measured
revisit_triggers: ledger-versus-measurement gaps that trend rather than scatter, indicating a metering, efficiency or discipline problem

base.update_signal: reconciliation gaps between ledger and measurement, and any change in how the run-handling KB's job record consumes the electrical column

nodes.definition: Measurement closes the loop, and the first article is where it closes cheapest. Before the remainder of a batch plates, the first piece is measured by XRF (ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 method class): at the mapped worst low-current-density point, at the named high-wear points, and at three or more points overall so a single lucky flat cannot pass the piece. Method honesty is part of the node: XRF calibration must match the actual stack and base - gold over nickel over brass is a different measurement problem than gold over silver, and a mismatched calibration reads confidently wrong; very thin flash sits near the method floor; and curved, tiny or recessed surfaces challenge the spot. Where XRF cannot see, the witness coupon carries the verification. A first article on target releases the batch to continue; a miss stops it - the error is corrected once, on one piece, instead of replicated across twenty. Measurement beats estimate every time they disagree; the estimate is then recalibrated, never defended.

included: first-article gating before batch continuation
worst-point and multi-point measurement
XRF method-class limits: stack calibration, thin-flash floor, spot geometry
excluded: full acceptance testing (adhesion, porosity, color - quality specialist)
customer-facing thickness claims (verification and marking specialists)

pros.claim: One measured piece before twenty plated ones converts batch-scale rework into a single trim
pros.example: the first ring reading under floor at the prong backs costs ten more minutes in the tank for one piece - discovered at final inspection instead, it costs a strip-and-replate day for the batch

cons.claim: XRF answers only where its calibration and geometry let it, and false confidence in a bad setup is worse than no reading
cons.example: measuring a gold-over-nickel-over-brass bead against a gold-over-copper calibration produces a fluent, wrong number - the stack model, not the instrument, was the error

failure_modes: measuring convenient flats and calling the piece verified
running a calibration that does not match the stack under the gold
letting the batch continue while the first article waits for a free moment at the instrument
acceptance_tests: the batch record shows a first-article reading at the mapped worst point and high-wear points against a stack-matched calibration before any further piece entered the tank
revisit_triggers: the stack changes (calibration must follow)
first-article results repeatedly contradict coupon or ledger evidence, questioning the instrument setup

base.update_signal: disagreement between XRF, coupon and ledger on the same load, or a stack change that invalidates the current calibration set

nodes.definition: The coupon methods are the cross-check class that keeps XRF honest and calibrates the tank. A witness coupon - a small piece of known area, same base and stack logic as the work - rides the rack through the same run, and afterward yields the tank's real behavior two ways: weight gain divided by area and gold's density gives the average thickness actually deposited, and an XRF reading on the coupon's flat, ideal surface gives the instrument a best-case check. Weight gain integrates over the whole coupon, so it complements point-reading XRF: together they separate 'the tank deposited less than estimated' from 'the deposit went somewhere other than the measurement point'. The coupon's placement rule is the method's honesty clause: it must ride at representative current density - a coupon parked in a hot corner calibrates a fiction. Coupon results are the preferred input for updating the tank's efficiency factor, because area and mass are both known precisely, which is exactly what the production pieces never offer.

included: witness coupon practice and placement honesty
weight-gain arithmetic to average thickness
coupon as the efficiency-factor calibration input
excluded: porosity, adhesion and wear testing on coupons (quality specialist)
coupon-based bath analysis programs (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: A coupon gives the one measurement where area, mass and conditions are all actually known
pros.example: a flat coupon of measured area weighed before and after the run pins the tank's deposition rate at these settings - the number every future Faraday estimate quietly depends on

cons.claim: The coupon measures the tank, not the piece - a perfect coupon coexists with a starved recess two hooks away
cons.example: coupon-average thickness on target while the pendant bail interior sits thin is not a contradiction; it is exactly why worst-point XRF and coupon methods are run together

failure_modes: parking the coupon in a corner of the rack whose density represents nothing
using a coupon base or stack unlike the work and calibrating the wrong system
skipping the pre-weigh and losing the weight-gain arithmetic entirely
acceptance_tests: coupon records show pre- and post-weights, known area, rack position, and the efficiency-factor update or confirmation they produced
revisit_triggers: coupon and first-article XRF disagree beyond their combined honesty bands

base.update_signal: systematic coupon-versus-XRF divergence, or a work-mix change that makes the current coupon base unrepresentative

nodes.definition: The delivered micron has a price, and the mechanism is plain: deposited gold mass equals area times thickness times gold's density of 19.3 g/cm3 (scaled by deposit purity), so every micron of overshoot across a load is bought metal that the quote may not carry, and every micron of undershoot is a spec failure whose remedy - re-run or strip-and-replate - spends gold, time and risk twice. The honest trim lives between those cliffs: size the run to reach the verified floor at the mapped worst point, let the first article show where above floor the easy zones landed, and tighten the overshoot batch by batch as the efficiency factor and distribution knowledge sharpen in the log. Two hard boundaries frame the node: the spec floor is never traded for gold savings - trimming happens above the measured floor or not at all - and thickness is never converted into a wear-life promise, because wear claims belong to the verification and marking specialists with measurement behind them. Pricing the job, and the drag-out losses that dwarf overshoot in a sloppy shop, belong to the business and run-handling KBs.

included: mass equals area times thickness times density as the overshoot cost mechanism
undershoot as double-spend rework
trim-above-verified-floor discipline
excluded: job pricing and quoting (business specialist)
drag-out and recovery economics (run-handling KB)
wear-life claims (verification and marking specialists)

pros.claim: Knowing the mass arithmetic makes overshoot a visible line item instead of invisible generosity
pros.example: a batch of bangles run a half micron over floor across their large area is a quantifiable gold spend - seeing it as grams focuses the trim effort where area is biggest

cons.claim: Aggressive trimming against an uncertain efficiency factor courts the far more expensive undershoot
cons.example: shaving the run time while the factor is one coupon old turns a modest gold saving into a strip-and-replate that costs more than a year of the saving

failure_modes: trimming run time below the verified floor to save gold
chasing overshoot before the efficiency factor and distribution map have earned trust
letting thickness slide into a wear-life promise to justify its cost
acceptance_tests: any trim decision cites the measured worst-point floor it preserves and the log evidence behind the factor it leans on
revisit_triggers: gold price movement or measured overshoot trends that change where the trim effort pays

base.update_signal: measured overshoot trend across the log and any undershoot incident traced to a trim decision

nodes.definition: The stop rule that keeps electrical ambition from damaging pieces or promises. Some geometries cannot be delivered as specified within this shop's equipment class: recesses the distribution map shows will never reach the floor even with the auxiliary-anode classes on hand, hollows no internal anode can enter, and pieces whose only contact points would leave visible damage that no wiring cleverness hides. For these, the answer is escalation to intake and the customer decision path - a respec to an achievable floor, a documented thin-zone or contact-mark waiver, referral to a shop with the capability, or refusal - never forcing the piece onto the line and never a quiet delivery of less than the words on the job sheet. The escalation is documented: what the map showed, which mitigations were tried or ruled out (repositioning, shields, robbers, each auxiliary class), and where the honest limit sits, so intake negotiates from evidence. Contact-damage judgment shares a border with fixturing - who can physically hold the piece is their question; whether any holdable arrangement can deliver the spec is this one.

included: the cannot-deliver triggers: unreachable floors, unenterable hollows, damage-only contacts
the escalation outputs: respec, waiver, referral, refusal
documenting the attempted mitigations
excluded: conducting the customer conversation (intake specialist)
rack engineering to create new contact options (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: A formal stop rule converts the worst jobs from future disputes into informed decisions
pros.example: the filigree locket whose interior can never see current leaves intake with a signed exterior-only waiver instead of returning in a month as a complaint

cons.claim: Escalation has a real cost in delay and occasionally in a lost job, which tempts quiet compromise
cons.example: sending the awkward heirloom back to intake feels worse than 'doing one's best' - until the undisclosed thin zone wears through on a piece that cannot be replaced

failure_modes: forcing contact on a piece that cannot take it and shipping the damage as 'character'
silently delivering less than spec on geometry the shop knew it could not serve
escalating without the mitigation record, so intake renegotiates blind
acceptance_tests: every escalated job carries the map extract, the mitigations tried or ruled out, and the stated honest limit; no job proceeds against a known cannot-deliver finding without a documented customer decision
revisit_triggers: new auxiliary-anode capability or equipment changes what counts as deliverable
an escalation pattern shows a piece family worth building capability for

base.update_signal: escalation outcomes - which waivers customers accept, which referrals return - and any capability change that moves the deliverable line
